comparator.name: Arts, Culture and Media
comparator.route: Film and Music with Analysis and Criticism
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 TER defines a 180-EC bachelor. This pathway takes the compulsory Year-1 foundation, the first-listed faculty-wide choice, Film I and Music I; continues Film and Music in Year 2; selects Analysis and Criticism, the first-listed Year-2 faculty-wide choice, Film III, Narrativity Across Media and From Studio to Exhibition; and completes the 30-EC minor, Arts in Practice, Evaluating the Arts, Advanced Seminar Film and thesis. Film and Music are the first two eligible departmental disciplines; Analysis and Criticism represents the broad academic identity. Choices are independent of UCR fit.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Film and Music with Analysis and Criticism
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic programme requires two arts disciplines and one framework. Film and Music are the first two eligible departmental disciplines. Analysis and Criticism is the broad cross-arts framework, while Arts Policy and Cultural Entrepreneurship is more professionally specialised. Faculty-wide choices use official order as a neutral tie-break; no choice was made for UCR fit.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Business, economics, sociology and Western art history establish the organisational, economic, social and visual foundations in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes every selected course that formally requires it. Introductory sociology and art history precede modern sociology, advanced social theory and advanced museum and heritage work; Introduction to Film & Media precedes Media & Race. The final year consolidates cultural theory, media history and representation, literature, market research, art-historical writing and public rhetoric. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three alternatives are defensible and the maximum is reached. The closest match owns broad art-and-society, criticism, ethical, arts-education, cross-art and Analysis and Criticism interests (7666, 7670, 7671, 7673, 7674, 7678). Film/literature/media communication (7662, 7665, 7672, 7675) and arts policy/cultural entrepreneurship (7667-7669, 7679) yield distinct feasible curricula. Music (7663, 7676) and theatre/performance (7664, 7677) remain evidenced candidates but are not attempted after the maximum; UCR also lacks dedicated music and performance sequences. Curricular topics support the mapped core and candidates; illustrative and outcome rows remain search-only.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Open minor or study-abroad space has no universal content to match.
Optional independent research is shown here rather than treating a scheduled course as a thesis.
Both examine literature and imaginative culture as ways of making social worlds.
Both introduce audiovisual and media forms and cultural analysis.
Both develop close analysis of film as art and medium.
Both examine narratives across forms and cultural traditions.
Both apply theory to film; UCR focuses on documentary.
Both examine art’s public presentation, institutions and audiences.
Both examine relations between film, text and media; UCR focuses on adaptation and intermedial reading.
Both examine mediated identity and storytelling; UCR focuses on environmental media.
No unoccupied UCR course reproduces the dedicated film-history sequence.
UCR has no disciplinary music-history course.
The closest UCR narrative courses are already aligned elsewhere.
No unoccupied scheduled course reproduces the advanced Film seminar.
Both introduce sociological analysis of institutions and culture; UCR is broader than arts sociology.
Both combine reflection with public-facing multimedia production.
Both develop evidence-based critical judgement for public audiences.

notes.text: Groningen Arts, Culture and Media requires sequential study in Film and Music in this pathway, plus Analysis and Criticism, Arts in Practice and a thesis. UCR offers strong related study in film and media, literature, visual art and heritage, cultural analysis, sociology and communication, but it does not offer comparable music or theatre/performance sequences.
